newsitem.title: FRANCE: Zairean opposes trial for diplomat over deaths.
newsitem.headline: Zairean opposes trial for diplomat over deaths.

text.p: A Zairean official said on Tuesday he opposed letting Kinshasa's ambassador to Paris stand trial for killing two French boys with his car, but the French government renewed its vow to bring the envoy to justice.

Kititwa Tumansi, until Tuesday Zaire's deputy prime minister for foreign affairs, said in a radio interview that lifting the diplomatic immunity of Ambassador Ramazani Baya would leave diplomats everywhere vulnerable to prosecution.

"Ramazani Baya has himself expressed the desire to stand trial in France, but he cannot do this because immunity is not granted to the ambassador but granted to Zaire by France," Kititwa told Radio France Internationale.
Baya "is not above the law, but there is an agreement which protects all of the world's diplomats," he said.
Kinshasa named a new crisis cabinet on Tuesday which dropped Kititwa.
But whatever Kititwa's status, French Foreign Ministry spokesman Yves Doutriaux said Paris had not yet received a formal reply to its request that Baya's immunity be lifted.
"The French authorities are determined to pursue their efforts to obtain the lifting of Baya's diploamtic immunity," Doutriaux told Reuters.
"We are going to reiterate our position to the new minister," he said.

Baya was driving at more than twice the legal speed limit through the Riviera resort town of Menton a month ago when his car hit Raphael Lenoir, 13, and Ronald Lehartel, 12, on a pedestrian crossing, killing both, police said.
The boys' mothers are campaigning to bring Baya to trial for the accident.
"Diplomatic immunity exists so that diplomats can fulfil their mission, not so they can escape the law," French Foreign Minister Herve de Charette said on Monday after meeting the mothers.
Before being recalled by his government and leaving France for Kinshasa, Baya had offered to renounce his immunity, and Zairean President Mobutu Sese Seko later agreed the envoy should stand trial.
